sources.title: Balochistan Climate Change Policy
sources.organization: Government of Balochistan and UNDP Pakistan
sources.temporal_coverage: Provincial climate risks and 2022 flood/fire impacts discussed in a 2024 policy.
sources.methodology: Provincial policy developed with consultations across districts and sectoral planning.
sources.limitations: Policy synthesis, not an independent impact evaluation; recommendations are not evaluated capacity.

sources.title: Health Emergency Situation Report: Monsoon Floods, 25 July 2025
sources.organization: World Health Organization, Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean
sources.temporal_coverage: Monsoon and flash-flood impacts and health response reported as of 25 July 2025.
sources.methodology: Operational snapshot drawing on NDMA totals, PMD forecasts and health-sector reporting.
sources.limitations: Single-date situation update; early impact and response figures are not final outcome estimates.

sources.title: Pakistan: Acute Food Insecurity Analysis, December 2025–September 2026
sources.organization: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) Analysis Unit, Pakistan
sources.temporal_coverage: Analysis covers observed acute food insecurity in December 2025–March 2026; its April–September 2026 projection period had elapsed by this extraction.
sources.methodology: Current-period classification used a household Food Security and Livelihood Assessment from September–November 2025 and secondary sources.
sources.limitations: 45 districts were covered, fewer than the previous 68; this finding is historical.

claims.paraphrase: The policy says declining groundwater, recurring drought and heatwaves erode agriculture and displace vulnerable, resource-dependent rural communities, increasing poverty in Balochistan.
claims.limitations: Provincial policy framing; it does not quantify these pathways by district.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The foreword explicitly links climate shocks with displacement and rising poverty.

claims.paraphrase: The policy reports that rain-induced floods displaced over 1.3 million people in Balochistan in 2022; women, youth and vulnerable communities face disproportionate climate-related food and health risks.
claims.limitations: The policy gives a province-wide 2022 displacement figure without district breakdown.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: It connects the floods to displacement and climate shocks to unequal food and health risks.

claims.paraphrase: The policy says climate disasters combined with social norms obstruct women's access to healthcare, including transport, supplies, skilled staff and information.
claims.limitations: The passage describes provincial barriers but does not quantify service access by district.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The policy identifies social norms as compounding climate-related healthcare barriers.

claims.paraphrase: As of 25 July 2025, NDMA reported 266 deaths and 628 injuries from heavy rain and flash floods since 26 June; reported deaths included 144 in Punjab, 63 in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, 25 in Sindh and 16 in Balochistan.
claims.limitations: Dated situation totals during an ongoing monsoon season; not a final event tally.

claims.paraphrase: By 25 July 2025, health contingency plans and high-risk district control rooms were activated, medical supplies prepositioned, and partner mobile units had served over 3,000 people in Rawalpindi, Chakwal, Attock, Sargodha, Sohbatpur and Usta Muhammad.
claims.limitations: The report gives operational outputs, not independent outcome or coverage evaluation.

claims.paraphrase: IPC classified 7.5 million people (21%) in 45 rural districts of Balochistan, Sindh and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in Phase 3 or worse for December 2025–March 2026, citing residual monsoon floods, prolonged drought and localized insecurity as drivers.
affected_groups: people classified in IPC Phase 3 or worse
claims.limitations: Assessment-period finding; coverage was 45 districts, fewer than the prior analysis.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: IPC identifies insecurity alongside climate shocks as a driver of acute food insecurity.

claims.locator: Drivers and district findings, PDF pp. 2 and 6.
claims.paraphrase: IPC identifies localized insecurity as a main food-insecurity driver in Kachi and Tank, disrupting livelihoods, markets, services and income.
claims.limitations: The report describes insecurity as a food-insecurity driver, not as caused by climate hazards.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: It states insecurity disrupts local livelihoods and markets and contributes to food insecurity.

claims.paraphrase: The household assessment associated drought with income declines of 30% in Balochistan, 14% in Sindh and 9% in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa; respondents also reported water scarcity and reduced crop or livestock production.
claims.limitations: Survey-based assessment-period findings; the report does not establish future losses.

access_audit.notes: Official UNDP landing page identifies publication date 19 November 2024; publication date was not inferred from the PDF URL.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrases only.

access_audit.notes: Report dated 25 July 2025; as-of status and planned versus completed actions were retained.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrases only.

access_audit.notes: The report's April–September 2026 projection period had elapsed at access; claims use only the observed December 2025–March 2026 analysis.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrases only.

search_audit.outcome: Opened WHO's dated operational report and Balochistan's provincial climate policy; retained only dated, source-supported district or provincial findings.

search_audit.outcome: IPC directly names localized insecurity alongside drought and flood shocks in acute food insecurity; no climate-causes-armed-conflict link was established.

search_audit.outcome: IPC reports insecurity disrupting markets, livelihoods and services in Kachi and Tank; searches did not establish a climate driver of that insecurity.

search_audit.outcome: WHO reports activated health contingency plans, control rooms, prepositioned supplies and named mobile-clinic deployments; these are operational outputs, not outcome evaluations.

search_audit.outcome: UNHCR PDF was blocked (HTTP 429) and alternate mirror timed out; search-result text was excluded, so no refugee climate finding is claimed.

gaps: The accessed sources establish climate-related displacement, health and livelihood vulnerability, and localized insecurity as a separate food-insecurity driver; they do not establish that climate hazards caused armed conflict.
Balochistan policy findings are provincial and do not quantify district differences; WHO's July 2025 report is an early operational snapshot, not a final impact assessment.
IPC findings refer to its December 2025–March 2026 assessment period and cover 45 rural districts, fewer than its prior analysis; they are not current October 2026 estimates.
UNHCR's original Forced Displacement Survey PDF returned HTTP 429 and its alternate mirror timed out; no claims were taken from search snippets or the opened publisher summary.
